rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context can license an understood pronoun; al-Farrāʾ says this kind of omission is common in Arabic and poetry.
rows.anchor: فحسن الإضمار لما عرف. ومثله فى سورة الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted pronoun is unsuitable when the coordinated actions have no close semantic connection to identify what was left out.
rows.anchor: وأما ما لا يحسن فيه الضمير لقلة اجتماعه

rows.speaker: بعض بني أسد
rows.claim: An anonymous man of Banū Asad recited a horse poem as Arabic poetic evidence for the preceding construction.
rows.anchor: وأنشدني بعض بني أسد يصف فرسه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase says the trade profited although merchants, not trade itself, profit; the meaning is clear from the commercial context.
rows.anchor: كيف تربح التجارة وإنما يربح الرجل التاجر؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic idiom permits attributing profit or loss to a sale, as well as describing a night as sleeping or a matter as resolved.
rows.anchor: فحسن القول بذلك لأن الربح والخسران إنما يكونان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a gradual process, إلى can mark the interval between beginning and end; its sequential sense explains the use of fa in the construction.
rows.anchor: فصلحت الفاء في «إلى» لأنك

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī heard a Bedouin use إلى for the span between two events, from the moon's first appearance to its disappearance.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: سمعت أعرابيا ورأى الهلال

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī also reports the camel-tax phrase خمسًا إلى خمس وعشرين, meaning the span from five to twenty-five; shin becomes liable only at the threshold.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن بعض العرب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example means God used a likeness not everyone recognizes, by which some are led astray and others guided; only the defiantly disobedient are misled.
rows.anchor: ماذا أراد الله بمثل لا يعرفه كل أحد يضل به هذا ويهدي به هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How can you disbelieve is an exclamation of astonishment and rebuke, not a plain question.
rows.anchor: على وجه التعجب والتوبيخ لا على الاستفهام المحض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause means “when you had been dead”; qad is understood because both states have already occurred, as in other past-state constructions.
rows.anchor: المعنى- والله أعلم- وقد كنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading فأمتعه has a kasra on its initial hamza, like أَعْلَمُ in the cited analogy.
rows.anchor: «فأمتعه قليلا ثم أضطره» بكسر الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القواعد means the foundations of the House; قاعدة is its singular. قاعد describes a woman past menstruation, and قعيدة can mean a man's wife.
rows.anchor: ومن النساء اللواتي قد قعدن عن المحيض قاعد بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربنا تقبل منا has an understood يقولان; ʿAbd Allāh's reading makes that verb explicit.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله «ويقولان ربنا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads أرناهم مناسكهم, referring to the descendants; the canonical أرنا includes them with the speakers, as the following return to “among them” shows.
rows.anchor: وفى قراءة عبد الله: «وأرناهم مناسكهم» ذهب إلى الذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In سفه نفسه the definite noun is an accusative explanatory specification, interpreted as indefinite; similar constructions include بطرت معيشتها and ضقت به ذرعا.
rows.anchor: وهي من المعرفة كالنكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanatory accusative cannot be fronted: one cannot say رأيه سفه زيد, just as one cannot front دارا in the parallel construction.
rows.anchor: فلا يقال: رأيه سفه زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan copies read وأوصى in place of وصى; both forms are sound and frequent in Arabic.
rows.anchor: في مصاحف أهل المدينة «وأوصى» وكلاهما صواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويعقوب is a second subject: Jacob also enjoined this teaching.
rows.anchor: ويعقوب وصى بهذا أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh or Ubayy inserts أن before the address; the canonical reading omits it, since reported speech may take or omit أن.
rows.anchor: وفي إحدى القراءتين قراءة عبد الله أو قراءة أبي: «أن يا بني إن الله اصطفى لكم الدين»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preceding prohibition, الميتة والدم are nominative whether إنما is one particle with a passive verb or ما is relative and they predicate it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز هاهنا إلا رفع الميتة والدم لأنك إن جعلت «إنما»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is slaughtered for other than God is what was invoked for another deity at slaughter.
rows.anchor: الإهلال: ما نودي به لغير الله على الذباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير باغ ولا عاد is a circumstantial accusative, meaning neither transgressing nor exceeding necessity; the allowance is only what sustains life.
rows.anchor: (غير) في هذا الموضع حال للمضطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The desperate eater should not attack people, eat to excess, or take provisions; the dispensation only preserves life.
rows.anchor: ولا تحل الميتة للمضطر إذا عدا على الناس بسيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the phrase as asking what made them endure the Fire.
rows.anchor: فما الذي صبرهم على النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other reading is “how bold they are toward the Fire”; the judge's reported idiom ما أصبرك على الله supports this sense.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: سألني قاضي اليمن وهو بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause can be parsed with البر nominative and أن تولوا accusative, or البر accusative and the أن-clause nominative.
rows.anchor: إن شئت رفعت «البر» وجعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because one reading has ليس البر بأن, al-Farrāʾ prefers nominative البر; righteousness is not merely facing either prayer direction but faith and the ensuing virtues.
rows.anchor: فلذلك اخترنا الرفع في «البر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها, تديرونها may be accusative or nominative; an indefinite noun can take a verbal predicate in either position.
rows.anchor: تديرونها في موضع نصب فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite noun cannot be replaced by its verb as predicate in the same way, because a definite noun is specified while an indefinite one is open-ended.
rows.anchor: ولم يصلح ذلك في المعرفة لأن المعرفة موقتة معلومة

rows.speaker: المفضل الضبي
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī recited poetry with الحميم الحميم, where the second repeats and intensifies the first; without it, the first would be nominative.
rows.anchor: أفاطم إني هالك فتبيني ... ولا تجزعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وإن كان ذو عسرة, nominative ذو is possible; ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy instead read accusative ذا, implying an omitted subject of كان.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله وأبي «وإن كان ذا عسرة» فهما جائزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative with كان requires an understood, indefinite subject; the cited poetry supplies such a subject and illustrates the construction.
rows.anchor: لأن بنية (كان) على أن يكون لها مرفوع ومنصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the noun is overt, as in فإن كن نساء, the predicate can still be nominative or accusative, as in the cited trade construction.
rows.anchor: فإن كن نساء فوق اثنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In تكون ميتة, feminine agreement follows the semantic noun; in إن تك مثقال حبة, the verb likewise follows the understood حبة despite masculine مثقال.
rows.anchor: لأن المثقال أضيف إلى الحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry also lets a feminine verb agree with an implied feminine referent such as hand, death, or the plural hooked sticks.
rows.anchor: فأنث فعل الداعي وهو ذكر لأنه ذهب إلى الموتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا يضار الكاتب والشاهد means do not summon either while occupied.
rows.anchor: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد أي لا يدع كاتب وهو مشغول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid reads فرهن as the plural of رهان, just as ثمر can mean fruits.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فرهن على جمع الرهان كما قال كلوا من ثمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians allow قلبه in the accusative, by analogy with “you made your judgment foolish” and “you sinned your heart.”
rows.anchor: فإن يكن حقا فهو من جهة قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غفرانك is a verbal noun used as an imperative and is therefore accusative, like repeating الصلاة as a command.
rows.anchor: مصدر وقع في موضع أمر فنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other nouns can also stand accusative when an imperative is intended; a nominative as a statement is also possible and still carries command force.
rows.anchor: وجميع الأسماء من المصادر وغيرها إذا نويت الأمر نصبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وسعها is a noun meaning capacity; its vocalic pattern parallels the alternatives in وجد and جهد.
rows.anchor: الوسع اسم في مثل معنى الوجد والجهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On their sides is coordinated with the state nouns because it means lying down; على جنبه and لجنبه are equivalent.
rows.anchor: وعلى جنوبهم: ونياما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ينادي للإيمان means calling toward faith; Arabic can use ل in place of إلى, as in the cited guidance examples.
rows.anchor: كما قال: «الذي هدانا لهذا» و «أوحى لها» يريد إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' travel and success in gaining wealth should not deceive believers; Jews used to travel and acquire money.
rows.anchor: كانت اليهود تضرب في الأرض فتصيب الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متاع قليل means a brief worldly enjoyment.
rows.anchor: متاع قليل ... (197) في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نزلا and ثوابا explain what the believers receive, like calling something a gift, sale, or charity.
rows.anchor: لهم ذلك نزلا وثوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خاشعين لله means believing in God humbly.
rows.anchor: وقوله: خاشعين لله ... (199) معناه: يؤمنون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should endure with their Prophet in jihad and outlast their enemy in patience.
rows.anchor: مع نبيكم على الجهاد (وصابروا) عدوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا means that the women's selves willingly consent; the verb shifts from selves to women, leaving نفسا as an explanatory accusative.
rows.anchor: فإن طبن لكم عن شيء منه نفسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نفسا is singular in this construction, though a plural form would also be correct; the same subject shift appears in ضاق به ذرعا and قررت به عينا.
rows.anchor: ولذلك وحد النفس. ولو جمعت لكان صوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السفهاء refers to women and children; قياما means the property through which people are sustained, and Nāfiʿ's قيما has the same meaning.
rows.anchor: النساء والصبيان التي جعل الله لكم قياما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For plural women, Arabic more often uses اللاتي than التي; for plural possessions and other things it more often uses التي.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول في جمع النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آنستم means found or recognized; ʿAbd Allāh's reading is أحستم.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله «فإن أحستم منهم رشدا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم addresses the guardians and the orphans.
rows.anchor: فادفعوا إليهم أموالهم يعني الأوصياء واليتامى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وبدارا أن يكبروا is an accusative verbal noun meaning do not hasten to consume the property before they come of age.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وبدارا أن يكبروا (أن) في موضع نصب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor guardian may eat بالمعروف as a loan.
rows.anchor: فليأكل بالمعروف هذا الوصى. يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نصيبا مفروضا is accusative because مفروضا is taken as a verbal-noun-like specification; if it were an ordinary noun it would not be accusative.
rows.anchor: وإنما نصب النصيب المفروض وهو نعت للنكرة لأنه أخرجه مخرج المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protection command requires returning the polytheist to his place of safety.
rows.anchor: يقول: رده إلى موضعه ومأمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional verb remains jussive though أحد separates إن from it; إن uniquely permits such separation because it is a particle rather than a noun.
rows.anchor: في موضع جزم وإن فرق بين الجازم والمجزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other intervening nominative or accusative words are likewise possible with إن; the cited verse and poetic line illustrate this looseness.
rows.anchor: وذلك سهل في (إن) خاصة دون حروف الجزاء

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows an accusative object before the jussive response but rejects a nominative subject in that position, since the response verb recalls its subject.
rows.anchor: وكان الكسائي يجيز تقدمة النصب في جواب الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ rejects al-Kisāʾī's exception: a conditional answer must take fa, or an equivalent jussive; without fa, a noun must contain the implied fa.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك كما قال لأن الجزاء له جواب بالفاء

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī cites a poem in which الخير appears accusative after a jussive conditional, but al-Farrāʾ parses it as an adjective of الأيام and reads تعقب as feminine.
rows.anchor: وكان الكسائي يجيز تقدمة النصب في جواب الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قطع من الليل refers to the darkness at the end of night.
rows.anchor: والقطع ظلمة آخر الليل فأسر بأهلك بقطع من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فزيلنا is a causative form meaning We separated them; فزايلنا is a variant reading, and Arabic often treats فاعل and فعل alike unless reciprocity is intended.
rows.anchor: ليست من زلت إنما هي من زلت ذا من ذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading تتلو, reported from ʿAbd Allāh, means each soul reads its record; verses about receiving and reading one's book support it.
rows.anchor: قرأها عبد الله بن مسعود: (تتلو) بالتاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid's تبلو reading means a person is shown or informed of what they did; al-Farrāʾ says this reading is also sound.
rows.anchor: وقرأها مجاهد (تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also read تبلو and glossed it as informing; the report reaches him through al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس: (تبلو) تخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In مولاهم الحق, الحق may modify God, be an accusative adverb meaning truly, or describe their master as true.
rows.anchor: (الحق) تجعله من صفات الله تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same three grammatical interpretations of الحق apply in فذلكم الله ربكم الحق.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قراءة أهل المدينة has كلمات ربك in the plural, alongside the singular كلمة ربك.
rows.anchor: قراءة أهل المدينة على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون can mean it is decreed against them because or on account of their refusal to believe; the clause is accusative after a dropped preposition.
rows.anchor: حقت عليهم لانهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فصبر جميل is nominative as a noun phrase; فصبرا جميلا is also possible as a direct command to oneself, and Ubayy reads the accusative form.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (فصبر جميل) مثل قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا بشرى and يا بشراي reflect dialectal variation: some Qays and Hudhayl speakers keep alif, while first-person possessive alif can become doubled yāʾ.
rows.anchor: بنصب الياء، وهي لغة في بعض قيس

rows.speaker: القاسم بن معن
rows.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn recites a poem illustrating the yāʾ form in first-person speech.
rows.anchor: أنشدني القاسم بن معن: تركوا هوي وأعنقوا لهواهم ...

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal's poem, recited through a Banū Sulaym informant, supplies a dialectal example with first-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: أنشدني المفضل: يطوف بي عكب في معد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا بشرى with a still alif can be treated like يا بني, a singular vocative carrying a possessive sense; يا نفس اصبري likewise can address oneself.
rows.anchor: بالسكون فهو كقولك: يا بني لا تفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا بشراي is accusative; changing the final alif to yāʾ in يا بشري reflects the kasra required before first-person possessive yāʾ.
rows.anchor: فأضاف وغير الألف إلى الياء فإنه طلب الكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qabs is a piece of fire carried at the tip of a stick or reed.
rows.anchor: القبس مثل النار في طرف العود أو في القصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هُدًى means a guide; the verbal noun stands in for the active participle, and Moses had lost the way.
rows.anchor: يعني هاديا. فأجزأ المصدر من الهادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the call addressed to Moses, إني أنا ربك begins with kasra; the readings also allow the call to encompass أني and موسى.
rows.anchor: إن جعلت النداء واقعا على (موسى) كسرت (إني أنا ربك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses was told to remove sandals made from the hide of a dead donkey.
rows.anchor: ذكر أنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت فأمر بخلعهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طوى with kasra is normally declined; as a place-name it may be indeclinable, like Ḥunayn when understood as a town.
rows.anchor: ووجه الكلام (الإجراء إذا كسرت الطاء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet leaves حنين and جبل حراء uninflected when treating each as a place-name; with ḍamma, طوى is usually declined but can also be indeclinable.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر في ترك إجرائه: نصروا نبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading وأنا اخترتك attaches to نودي; اخترناك is also read, while إنا اخترناك with kasra starts a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ [وأنا اخترناك] مردودة على [نودي]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لذكرا may be read with alif as a verbal noun; alternatively the alif represents possessive yāʾ for rhyme, or a vocative lament yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: (لذكرا) بالألف فمن قال (ذكرا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers have أكاد أخفيها; Ubayy adds that God conceals the Hour even from Himself, while Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's أخفيها means reveal it, since خفي can mean reveal or hide.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي (إن الساعة آتية أكاد أخفيها من نفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command that God's earth is spacious addresses Meccan Muslims living among polytheists and means they should move to Medina rather than remain among unbelievers.
rows.anchor: يقول (إن أرضي واسعة) يعني المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading لنبوئنهم means We will settle them in dwellings; Ibn Masʿūd and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read لنثوينهم, “settle them” in the sense of staying.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق أن ابن مسعود قرأها (لنثوينهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The migration verse reassured Meccan believers who feared having no homes or livelihood in Medina; creatures do not store provisions, except ants.
rows.anchor: لما أمروا بالتحول عنها والخروج إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is حياة لا موت فيها, life with no death.
rows.anchor: وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان [64] حياة لا موت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In danger at sea, people direct sincere prayer and worship to God, then return to idols once rescued.
rows.anchor: يقول: يخلصون الدعاء والتوحيد إلى الله في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read وليتمتعوا with a jussive lām as command and rebuke; the Hijaz reading has a kasra for purpose, “so they may enjoy.”
rows.anchor: قرأها عاصم والأعمش على جهة الأمر والتوبيخ بجزم اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ordinarily refers to people, but it can refer to animals when they are explicated in human terms, as in the she-camel and creatures walking on their bellies.
rows.anchor: «من» إنما تكون للناس، فلما فسرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance set in the earth is justice.
rows.anchor: الميزان (7) . في الأرض وهو العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads وخفض الميزان; lowering and setting the balance are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: وخفض الميزان، والخفض والوضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading omits أن and has لا تطغوا in the scale.
rows.anchor: لا تطغوا بغير أن في الوزن وأقيموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألا تطغوا can be jussive as a prohibition or accusative after أن; al-Farrāʾ prefers the jussive because an imperative follows.
rows.anchor: في موضع جزم أحب إلي لأن بعدها أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was set out for all creatures.
rows.anchor: الأرض وضعها للأنام (10) . لجميع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads الريحان in the genitive, while other readers have nominative; genitive makes it another ذو phrase and nominative coordinates it with ذو.
rows.anchor: فمن خفض أراد: ذو العصف وذو الريحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The عصف is the crop foliage cut before ripening; الريحان is provision, and الحب is the edible grain.
rows.anchor: بقل الزرع لان العرب تقول: خرجنا نعصف الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says عصف is the edible part of grain, while الريحان is the sound part not yet eaten.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ذو العصف المأكول من الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hypothetical reading الحب ذا العصف والريحان is grammatical and means creating both; it appears in Syrian codices, though al-Farrāʾ knows no reader of it.
rows.anchor: ولو قرأ قارئ: «والحب ذا العصف والريحان»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning was revealed on the Prophet's arrival in Medina: buyers took extra measure or weight, sellers shorted them; they stopped and became exceptionally accurate.
rows.anchor: نزلت أول قدوم النبي صلى الله عليه إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say ويل is a valley in Hell; al-Farrāʾ distinguishes that report from the familiar word ويل.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن «ويل» واد في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In كالوهم/وزنوهم the suffix is an accusative object with a benefactive sense, equivalent to measured for them; a Hijazi Bedouin woman's usage confirms it.
rows.anchor: تقول: قد كلتك طعاما كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اكتالوا على الناس means “took from people”; على and من alternate because the amount is owed to them, though the prepositions emphasize different sides of the transaction.
rows.anchor: وهما تعتقبان: على ومن- في هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم يقوم الناس is an explanatory genitive for the day; because a preposition is omitted it can attach to مبعوثون, or be coordinated with the earlier يوم.
rows.anchor: هو تفسير اليوم المخفوض لما ألقي اللام من الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Sijjīn is a stone beneath the earth; al-Farrāʾ prefers it as a description, since a proper name would not decline, though it can decline if it means the inscribed stone.
rows.anchor: ونرى أنه صفة من صفاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their many sins surrounded and covered their hearts; a report from ʿUmar similarly says debt had enveloped al-Asyfaʿ's property.
rows.anchor: كثرت المعاصي والذنوب منهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses kanūd as ungrateful to his Lord: he counts his sins and forgets blessings.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: «إن الإنسان لربه لكنود» قال: لوام لربه يعد المسيئات، وينسى النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنه على ذلك لشهيد means God witnesses this about the human being.
rows.anchor: يقول: وإن الله على ذلك لشهيد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets شديد as miserly, and الخير as wealth.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي بإسناده: لشديد: لبخيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the person strong in love of wealth; al-Farrāʾ prefers “intense in love for wealth,” with الحب omitted after being stated once and for rhyme.
rows.anchor: ونرى والله أعلم- أن المعنى: وإنه للخير لشديد الحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted-love construction parallels عاصف describing the wind in the preceding phrase, though the word is attached to day for rhyme.
rows.anchor: والعصوف لا يكون للأيام إنما يكون للريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's codex reads بحث for بعثر; a Banū Asad Bedouin read بحثر, and both forms are dialectal.
rows.anchor: في مصحف عبد الله: «إذا بحث ما في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحصل ما في الصدور means what is hidden in the chests is made manifest.
rows.anchor: وحصل ما في الصدور (10) بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading is بأنه يومئذ بهم خبير.
rows.anchor: قراءة عبد الله: «بأنه يومئذ بهم خبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general warning about the slanderer was revealed about one particular man; Arabic may state a general rule while aiming at one interlocutor.
rows.anchor: وإنما نزلت في رجل واحد كان يهمز الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading is ويل للهمزة اللمزة.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله: «ويل للهمزة اللمزة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar read جمع with gemination; ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ, and al-Ḥasan read it light.
rows.anchor: ثقل : جمع. الأعمش وأبو جعفر المدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All read وعدده with gemination, meaning he counted and kept track of his wealth; al-Ḥasan's light reading was glossed by some as counting his clan.
rows.anchor: واجتمعوا جميعا على (وعدده) بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أخلده means “will make him live forever”; the past form can express a future result, as when one says a sinner entered Hell meaning Hell is due for him.
rows.anchor: يحسب أن ماله أخلده (3) يريد: يخلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has a singular subject in لينبذن; al-Ḥasan alone reads it intending both the man and his wealth.
rows.anchor: قرأها العوام: «لينبذن» على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحطمة is a name for Hell, like Jahannam, Saqar, and Laza; without the article it would be indeclinable as a proper name.
rows.anchor: والحطمة: اسم من أسماء النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تطلع على الأفئدة means its pain reaches the hearts; طلوع and بلوغ can share the sense of reaching.
rows.anchor: يقول: يبلغ ألمها الأفئدة، والاطلاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مؤصدة means shut or sealed, and it may be pronounced with or without hamza.
rows.anchor: وهي المطبقة، تهمز ولا تهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and other reciters among al-Farrāʾ's companions read في عمد with accusative عمد.
rows.anchor: كان أصحابنا يقرءون: (في عمد) بالنصب، وكذلك الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى means they exchanged guidance for error; buying one thing with another is fundamentally an exchange.
rows.anchor: أن من اشترى شيئا بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase makes trade profit although profit belongs to its participants; this is figurative language, like saying the matter was resolved.
rows.anchor: والتجارة لا تربح، وإنما يربح فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave them commands, they accepted and pledged to keep them, then broke the covenant by casting it aside and failing to act on it.
rows.anchor: أمرهم بأمور فقبلوها عنه، وذلك أخذ الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما أصبرهم means “how bold they are toward the Fire.”
rows.anchor: على النار} ما أجرأهم.

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī relays a judge's idiom ما أصبرك على الله, said to a man who swore away another's right, as evidence for “how bold.”
rows.anchor: عن الكسائي أنه قال: أخبرني قاضي اليمن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid's “how capable they are of the deeds of the people of the Fire” is a good reading, with deeds omitted and endurance understood.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: ما أصبرهم على النار، ما أعملهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes ما as “what thing made them endure the Fire and brought them to it,” not as an exclamation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: ما أصبرهم على النار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means pour patience over us as one pours from a bucket.
rows.anchor: أي صبه علينا، كما يفرغ الدلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وليّه means the guardian of the party whose right is owed.
rows.anchor: فليملل وليه بالعدل} أي] : ولي الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تضل means that one woman forgets the testimony and the other reminds her; Moses' phrase uses ضالّ for forgetful.
rows.anchor: أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} أي: تنسى إحداهما الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تسأموا means do not grow tired.
rows.anchor: ولا تسأموا} أي: لا تملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written record should include the debt whether it is small or large.
rows.anchor: أن تكتبوه صغيرا} من الدين كان {أو كبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقسط means more just; the record strengthens testimony because it reminds witnesses of all they witnessed.
rows.anchor: وأقوم للشهادة} لأن الكتاب يذكر الشهود جميع ما شهدوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أدنى ألا ترتابوا means less likely to doubt.
rows.anchor: وأدنى ألا ترتابوا} أي: أن لا تشكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present trade means goods the parties buy and sell among themselves.
rows.anchor: تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم} أي: تتبايعونها بينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writer must not be made to record what was not dictated, nor the witness to testify without being summoned; another view says they may refuse a summons.
rows.anchor: ولا يضار كاتب} فيكتب ما لم يملل عليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Kalbī explain لا يضار as not bothering a writer by distracting him from his trade or work.
rows.anchor: هذا قول مجاهد (1) والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رهن is the plural of رهان; the reading رهان is therefore a plural formed from an already plural form.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ (فرهن مقبوضة) أراد جمع "رهان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صابروا means persist against your enemy.
rows.anchor: اصبروا وصابروا} أي صابروا عدوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رباط originally meant opposing forces tying and preparing their horses at a frontier; residence at the frontier consequently came to be called ribāṭ.
rows.anchor: أن يربط هؤلاء خيولهم، ويربط هؤلاء خيولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تفلحون means winning enduring, everlasting life; falāḥ originally means remaining.
rows.anchor: تفلحون} أي: تفوزون ببقاء الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ابتلوا means test them.
rows.anchor: وابتلوا اليتامى} أي: اختبروهم. {حتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بلغوا النكاح means reaching the age when they can marry women.
rows.anchor: بلغوا النكاح} أي: بلغوا أن ينكحوا النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آنستم means you recognized or became certain; its root sense is seeing.
rows.anchor: علمتم وتبينتم. وأصل آنست: أبصرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بِدارا أن يكبروا means consuming the assets hurriedly before the orphans grow up and reclaim them.
rows.anchor: مبادرة أن يكبروا فيأخذوها منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian should refrain from eating the property; a poor guardian may eat moderately without extravagance.
rows.anchor: فليستعفف} أي: ليترك ولا يأكل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوزارهم means their sins; the root word الوزر is a load carried on the back, as in God removing a burden that weighed heavily.
rows.anchor: وأصل الوزر: الحمل على الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not mix faith with shirk; Luqmān calls shirk a great injustice.
rows.anchor: إيمانهم بظلم} أي: لم يخلطوه بشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forbidden paths veer away from God's straight path to its right or left; an Arab saying urges staying on the road and avoiding side tracks.
rows.anchor: يريد السبل التي تعدل عنه يمينا وشمالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means pour patience over us.
rows.anchor: أفرغ علينا صبرا} أي صبه علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نستبق means competing in archery; سبق can refer to the stake or prize.
rows.anchor: ننتضل، يسابق بعضنا بعضا في الرمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وما أنت بمؤمن لنا means you do not believe or trust us.
rows.anchor: بمؤمن لنا} أي: بمصدق لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بدم كذب means with blood falsely attributed to Joseph, or fabricated blood.
rows.anchor: على قميصه بدم كذب} أي: مكذوب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سولت means adorned or made attractive, as in Satan's making their deeds seem attractive.
rows.anchor: قال بل سولت} أي: زينت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الباقيات الصالحات is said to mean the five prayers.
rows.anchor: يقال: الصلوات الخمس. ويقال: سبحان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view glosses الباقيات الصالحات as the phrases “Glory be to God,” “Praise be to God,” and the other statements of remembrance listed.
rows.anchor: ويقال: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خير أملا means the best thing you can hope for.
rows.anchor: وخير أملا} أي خير ما تؤملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آنست نارا means I saw a fire; elsewhere the same verb means I knew or recognized, as in the orphan verse.
rows.anchor: أبصرت. وتكون في موضع آخر: علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فيدمغه means he smashes it; the root concerns striking the head or brain, a fatal blow.
rows.anchor: أصل هذا إصابة الرأس والدماغ بالضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زاهق means departing and disappearing.
rows.anchor: هو زاهق} أي زائل ذاهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جذوة means a piece of firewood; it is like جذمة, and exegesis describes it as a stick that has burned.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة منها. ومثلها الجذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لنبوئنهم means We will settle them in dwellings.
rows.anchor: من الجنة غرفا} أي لننزلنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative لنثوينهم derives from ثويت بالمكان, meaning I stayed there.
rows.anchor: فهو من "ثويت بالمكان" أي أقمت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وهنا على وهن means weakness upon weakness.
rows.anchor: على وهن} أي ضعفا على ضعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فصاله means his weaning.
rows.anchor: وهنا على وهن} أي ضعفا على ضعف. {وفصاله} فطامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust means the religious obligations; the heavens, earth, and mountains were offered them with their reward and punishment, then the human accepted.
rows.anchor: يعني: الفرائض. {على السماوات والأرض والجبال}

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes tell that Adam near death asked whom to appoint after him; told to offer his succession to all creation, he did so and all refused except his children.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: "إن آدم لما حضرته الوفاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balance God set is justice on earth.
rows.anchor: الميزان} أي العدل في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القسط means justice, and تخسروا الميزان means reduce the weight.
rows.anchor: بالقسط} أي بالعدل. {ولا تخسروا الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمشاج means mixtures: the man's fluid mixed with the woman's fluid; مشيج is a mixed thing.
rows.anchor: مشجته فهو مشيج. يريد: اختلاط ماء الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نبتليه means We test him; God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him through them.
rows.anchor: نختبره. أي إنا جعلناه سميعا بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كالوهم and وزنوهم mean they measured or weighed for them; Arabic uses the recipient suffix directly where لك is meant.
rows.anchor: يقال: كلتك ووزنتك؛ بمعنى: كلت لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يخسرون means they shortchange people.
rows.anchor: وكذلك: عددتك وعددت لك. {يخسرون} ينقصون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير ممنون means not cut off.
rows.anchor: غير ممنون} أي غير مقطوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كنود means deeply ungrateful; barren land is also called kanūd because it grows nothing.
rows.anchor: "الأرض الكنود": التي لا تنبت شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is his mother because he takes refuge in it as one returns to a mother.
rows.anchor: هاوية} أي النار له كالأم يأوي إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do good works have their reward undiminished.
rows.anchor: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} فإنهم غير منقوصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ويزكيهم means purify them; زكية in the other verse means purified.
rows.anchor: أي يطهرهم، قال: «نفسا زكية»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سفه نفسه means he ruined and destroyed himself; Arabic also says سفهت نفسك.
rows.anchor: أي أهلك نفسه وأوبقها، تقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اصطفى لكم الدين means He made the religion pure for you, from the root صفوة.
rows.anchor: أي أخلص لكم الدين، من الصفوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم after a completed statement is a new alternative or correction, not the interrogatives هل or hamza; al-Akhṭal's verse illustrates this.
rows.anchor: «أم» تجيء بعد كلام قد انقطع، وليست في موضع هل

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhṭal's verse exemplifies أم following a statement that has ended; it can be paraphrased “did you see?” or “rather, you saw.”
rows.anchor: قال الأخطل: كذبتك عينك أم رأيت بواسط ... غلس الظلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can call a paternal or maternal uncle a father.
rows.anchor: والعرب تجعل العم والخال أبا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A report about the Prophet at the conquest says he feared Quraysh might treat his father as Thaqīf had treated ʿUrwa; the Prophet had sent ʿUrwa to invite Thaqīf to Islam, where he was killed.
rows.anchor: قال حماد بن زيد عن أيوب، عن عكرمة: إن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وما أهل به means what was intended for sacrifice to another; another reading is what was named for their gods rather than God.
rows.anchor: «وما أهل به» (173) أي وما أريد به، وله مجاز آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith's use of استهل for an animal that neither drank, ate, nor cried points to making its first cry or sound.
rows.anchor: أرايت من لا شرب ولا أكل ولا صاح فاستهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير باغ ولا عاد means neither seeking forbidden food when not compelled nor exceeding the needed amount.
rows.anchor: «غير باغ ولا عاد» (173) أي لا يبغي فيأكله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is relative here: “what made them endure the Fire and called them to it”; this is not an exclamation.
rows.anchor: «ما» في هذا الموضع في معنى الذي، فمجازها:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source makes the verbal noun البر describe the person who believes; the sense is ولكن البار من آمن بالله, supported by al-Nābigha's usage.
rows.anchor: فالعرب تجعل المصادر صفات، فمجاز البر هاهنا

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's line supplies poetic evidence for using a verbal noun as an adjective.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة: وقد خفت حتى ما تزيد مخافتي ... على وعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الملأ are the leading men and notables.
rows.anchor: «الملإ من بني إسرائيل» (246) : وجوههم، وأشرافهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After Badr, the Prophet reportedly called Quraysh's leaders the elite; their deeds would have dwarfed an Anṣārī's comparison with killing bald old women.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما رجعوا من بدر سمع رجلا من الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هل عسيتم means “do you expect that you will do it?”
rows.anchor: هل تعدون أن تفعلوا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بسطة in knowledge and body means added measure, excellence, and abundance.
rows.anchor: «بسطة في العلم والجسم» (247) أي زيادة، وفضلا وكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آية means signs and proofs.
rows.anchor: «إن في ذلك لآية» (247) : علامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مبتليكم بنهر means testing you with a river.
rows.anchor: «مبتليكم بنهر» (249) : مختبركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غرفة can be a verbal noun; غُرفة can mean a handful or palmful.
rows.anchor: الغرفة مصدر، والغرفة: ملء الكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يظنون أنهم ملاقوا الله means they are certain they will meet God.
rows.anchor: «يظنون أنهم ملاقوا الله» (249) يوقنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فئة means a group.
rows.anchor: «يظنون أنهم ملاقوا الله» (249) يوقنون. «فئة» (249) : جماعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفرغ علينا صبرا means send patience down upon us.
rows.anchor: «أفرغ علينا صبرا» (250) : أنزل علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلة is the verbal noun of خليل and can itself mean a close friend; Awfā ibn Maṭar uses it in a poem.
rows.anchor: مصدر الخليل، وتقول: فلان خلتى

rows.speaker: أوفى بن مطر المازني
rows.claim: Awfā ibn Maṭar's poem uses خلة as a close friend.
rows.anchor: قال أوفى بن مطر المازني: ألا أبلغا خلتي جابرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تضل إحداهما means that one of the two forgets.
rows.anchor: «أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى» (282) أي تنسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A witness who has already testified must not refuse a summons; before witnessing, the person may choose not to testify.
rows.anchor: قال فيمن شهد: لا يأب إذا دعي، وله قبل أن يشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقسط means more just.
rows.anchor: «أقسط عند الله» (282) أعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فسوق means sin in this context.
rows.anchor: الفسوق: المعصية فى هذا الموضع

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr says رهان is used for horse-race stakes and cites a poem about pledging them.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: الرهان في الخيل، وأنشد

rows.speaker: قعنب بن أم صاحب
rows.claim: Qanʿab's poem uses رهن for a stake or wager.
rows.anchor: وأنشد قول قعنب بن أم صاحب من بني عبد الله بن غطفان: بانت سعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غفرانك means Your forgiveness, or “forgive us.”
rows.anchor: «غفرانك» (285) : مغفرتك، أي اغفر لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إصر means a burden or binding tie; a covenant or kinship that attaches someone to another is an إصر, as in the expression آصرة رحم.
rows.anchor: الإصر الثقل وكل شىء عطفك على شىء من عهد

rows.speaker: الأبيرد
rows.claim: Al-Ubayrid's verse on فصرهن إليك explains it as “bring them together toward you.”
rows.anchor: وقال الأبيرد في قوله عزت قدرته: «فصرهن إليك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نزلا means reward; it can also mean a lodging or something provided as a place to settle, from the verb “I settled him.”
rows.anchor: «نزلا من عند الله» (198) أي ثوابا، ويجوز منزلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رابطوا means stand firm and persist.
rows.anchor: «ورابطوا» (200) أي اثبتوا ودوموا

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhṭal's poem uses ribāṭ for horses stationed and prepared, and for enduring shame among Banū Kulayb.
rows.anchor: قال الأخطل: ما زال فينا رباط الخيل معلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خِفتم means you became certain, not merely afraid; Laylā bint al-Ḥammās's poetry uses خافوا in that sense.
rows.anchor: مجازه: أيقنتم، قالت ليلى بنت الحماس

rows.speaker: ليلى بنت الحماس
rows.claim: Laylā bint al-Ḥammās's line uses خافوا to mean “be certain.”
rows.anchor: قالت ليلى بنت الحماس: قلت لكم خافوا بألف فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تعولوا means act unjustly, so أدنى ألا تعولوا means nearer to not oppressing; Arabic says علت على for treating someone unjustly.
rows.anchor: «ذلك أدنى ألا تعولوا» (3) أي أقرب ألا تجوروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صدقاتهن means their dowries, given willingly as the prescribed obligation.
rows.anchor: «وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة» (4) أي مهورهن عن طيب نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قيامًا is what sustains you; the word can also occur as قوام, with some speakers retaining the wāw and others dropping it after kasra.
rows.anchor: مصدر يقيمكم، ويجيء فى الكلام فى معنى قوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ابتلوا اليتامى means test the orphans.
rows.anchor: «وابتلوا اليتامى» (6) أي اختبروهم. «إسرافا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إسرافا means excess or extravagance.
rows.anchor: «إسرافا» (7) الإسراف: الإفراط. «وبدارا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وبدارا means taking the property hastily before the orphan reaches maturity and demonstrates sound judgment.
rows.anchor: «وبدارا» (7) أي مبادرة قبل أن يدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فليأكل بالمعروف means the guardian must not accumulate the property as capital; taʾaththul is acquiring a principal fortune, as in al-Aʿshā's poem.
rows.anchor: «فليأكل بالمعروف» (7) أي لا يتأثل مالا

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse witnesses the root أثلة for an established principal or foundation.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: ألست منتهيا عن نحت أثلتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نصيبا مفروضا is accusative because it has been taken out of the normal descriptive construction.
rows.anchor: نصب على الخروج من الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قولا سديدا means upright or deliberate speech.
rows.anchor: «قولا سديدا» (10) أي قصدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إخوة means two or more brothers: Arabic sometimes uses a plural form for a pair and a dual form for a group, as al-Rāʿī's poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: «فإن كان له إخوة» (12) أي أخوان فصاعدا

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Rāʿī's poem uses plural forms for a pair and dual forms for a group, illustrating number flexibility.
rows.anchor: قال الراعي: أخليد إن أباك ضاف وساده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقرب لكم نفعا means more beneficial or closer in benefit.
rows.anchor: «أقرب لكم نفعا» (12) أدنى نفعا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text says the meaning of الثمن and الربع here is one and the same.
rows.anchor: «والربع» والمعنى واحد (؟)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلالة in Arabic is a person with no inheriting father, son, or brother.
rows.anchor: «كلالة» (13) : كل من لم يرثه أب أو ابن أو أخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the highland dialect, هلم is invariant for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine; al-Aʿshā uses it for a group.
rows.anchor: هلم في لغة أهل العالية للواحد والاثنين والجميع من الذكر والأنثى سواء

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's poem uses هلم as an invitation to a group.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: وكان دعا قومه بعدها ... هلم إلى أمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najdi speech inflects هلم for gender and number; Hijazi speech has no verb هلممت behind the invariant form.
rows.anchor: وأهل نجد يقولون للواحد هلم، وللمرأة هلمي، وللاثنين هلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إملاق means loss of one's property and poverty; أملق فلان means his wealth went away, like أقفر.
rows.anchor: من ذهاب ما فى أيديكم يقال: أملق فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملة إبراهيم means Abraham's religion; one can ask “what religious community are you from?”
rows.anchor: «ملة إبراهيم حنيفا» (161) أي دين إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نسكي is the verbal noun of نسكت, “I performed sacrifice as devotion”; نسكية is the offering and نسك is a plural form.
rows.anchor: «ونسكي ومحياي» (162) وهو مصدر نسكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلائف means successive successors on earth; الشماخ's line uses أخلف for moving from dwelling to dwelling.
rows.anchor: «خلائف الأرض» (165) : واحدهم: خليفة فى الأرض بعد خليفة

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammākh's verse exemplifies أخلف from the root خلف.
rows.anchor: قال الشماخ [وهو الرجل المتكبر] : تصيبهم وتخطئنى المنايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربع means a dwelling, plural ربوع, or a tribe; رجل من ربعه means a man from his tribe.
rows.anchor: الربع: الدار والجميع ربوع، والربع أيضا: قبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فصبر جميل is nominative because جميل modifies الصبر; without the adjective, Arabs would use the accusative command صبرا.
rows.anchor: «فصبر جميل» (18) مرفوعان لأن «جميل» صفة للصبر

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz poem uses صبر جميل as a nominative noun phrase with an adjective.
rows.anchor: قال [الراجز] : يشكو إلى جملى طول السرى

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأثرم
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Athram heard someone recite صبرا جميل as a vocative, meaning “O Jamīl.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأثرم: سمعت من ينشد: صبرا جميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شروه means they sold him; when you sell something to someone else, you say اشتريته.
rows.anchor: «وشروه بثمن بخس» (20) أي باعوه، فإذا بعته أنت

rows.speaker: ابن مفرغ
rows.claim: Ibn Mufarrigh's poem uses شريت in the sense of “I sold.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن مفرغ: وشريت بردا ليتنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بخس means deficient or reduced; it is a verbal noun used adjectivally, as Arabic can do.
rows.anchor: وهو مصدر بخست فوصفوا به وقد تفعل العرب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دراهم معدودة is genitive by repetition or apposition to the preceding price phrase.
rows.anchor: «بثمن بخس دراهم معدودة» (20) جررته على التكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثواه is his lodging or the place he stayed; a generous host is called the mother or father of a guest's lodging.
rows.anchor: «أكرمي مثواه» (21) أي مقامه الذي ثواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جذوة is a thick piece of wood with no flame; its plural is الجذا, and Ibn Muqbil's poem uses the term.
rows.anchor: «أو جذوة من النار» (29) أي قطعة غليظة من الحطب

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's poem uses الجذا for large pieces of firewood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مقبل: باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها ... جزل الجذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right bank is the side or edge of the valley; شط also describes half the hump.
rows.anchor: «شاطئ الواد الأيمن» (30) شط الوادي هو ضغة الوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جان is one kind of snake among others; this verse likens the staff to a jinn-snake, while the other verse calls it a snake of that kind.
rows.anchor: وفي آية أخرى: «فإذا هي حية تسعى» (20/ 20) فالحيات أجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولم يعقب means he did not turn back; عقب عليه means returned to or retraced it.
rows.anchor: «ولم يعقب» (31) أي لم يرجع يقال: عقب على ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اسلك means insert or put in; سلكته and أسلكته are both used.
rows.anchor: «اسلك يدك في جيبك» (32) مجازه: أدخل وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فصاله means his weaning.
rows.anchor: «وفصاله» (14) أي فطامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Follow the path of whoever returns and repents to God; the text then shifts back to Luqmān's teaching.
rows.anchor: «واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي» (15) أي طريق من رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثقال حبة من خردل means the weight of a mustard seed.
rows.anchor: «يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل» (16) أي زنة حبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تصعر خدك means do not turn or avert your face arrogantly; الصعر is a disease that twists a camel's head or neck.
rows.anchor: «ولا تصعر خدك للناس» (18) مجازه: ولا تقلب وجهك

rows.speaker: عمرو بن حنى التغلبي
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Ḥannī's verse uses صعر خده for the arrogant turning of one's face.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن حنى التغلبي: وكنا إذا الجبار صعر خده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disease صعر afflicts a camel's neck or head, making it a fitting comparison for human arrogance.
rows.anchor: والصعر داء يأخذ البعير في عنقه أو رأسه فيشبه به الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تمش مرحا means do not walk proudly and boastfully.
rows.anchor: «ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا» (18) أي لا تمرح فى مشيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنكر الأصوات means the harshest or most detested of voices.
rows.anchor: «إن أنكر الأصوات» (19) أي أشد الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أتواصوا به means they mutually agreed on it or took it from one another; a dominant shared trait can seem as if a people advised one another to it.
rows.anchor: «أتواصوا به» (53) أتواطئوا عليه وأخذه بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتول عنهم means turn away from and leave them; Ḥuṣayn ibn Ḍamḍam's poetry uses ولى of a horseman departing.
rows.anchor: «فتول عنهم» (54) أي أعرض عنهم واتركهم

rows.speaker: حصين بن ضمضم
rows.claim: Ḥuṣayn ibn Ḍamḍam's verse describes a horseman leaving his companions and escaping.
rows.anchor: قال حصين بن ضمضم أما بنو عبس فإن هجينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذنوبا means a share or portion, as alqama's poem and the phrase أذنبة show; its root image is a full bucket.
rows.anchor: «فإن للذين ظلموا ذنوبا مثل ذنوب أصحابهم» (59) أي نصيبا

rows.speaker: علقمة بن عبدة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada's line uses ذنوب for a portion of generosity.
rows.anchor: قال علقمة بن عبدة: وفي كل يوم قد خبطت بنائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ذنوب and a سجل are types of bucket filled with water, the physical sense behind the share metaphor.
rows.anchor: وإنما أصلها من الدلو والذنوب والسجل واحد وهو ملء الدلو

rows.speaker: الفضل بن عباس بن عتبة بن أبي لهب
rows.claim: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās's poem depicts someone filling a bucket to the handle.
rows.anchor: قال الفضل بن عباس بن عتبة بن أبى لهب: من يساجلنى يساجل ماجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حسبان is a plural pattern like شهبان formed from شهاب; the verse describes the sun and moon by calculation.
rows.anchor: «الشمس والقمر بحسبان» (5) جميع حساب مثل شهبان وشهاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الشجر is vegetation with a trunk; النجم grows from the earth without a trunk, and the verb is dual to match the two nouns.
rows.anchor: «والنجم والشجر يسجدان» (6) الشجر ما كان على ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألا تطغوا في الميزان means do not commit injustice or reduce the measure.
rows.anchor: «ألا تطغوا في الميزان» (8) أن لا تظلموا وتنقصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تخسروا means do not wrong people or shortchange the measure; the opposite is fairness and justice.
rows.anchor: «ولا تخسروا» (9) أي لا تظلموا وتنقصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأنام means all created beings.
rows.anchor: «وضعها للأنام» (10) للخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أكمام means the sheaths or husks of date clusters; كم is singular.
rows.anchor: «والنخل ذات الأكمام» (11) واحدها كم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The عصف is the crop's leafy growth or upper ear, including the leaves that can be eaten; ʿAlqama's poem mentions its foliage.
rows.anchor: «والحب ذو العصف والريحان» (12) تخرج له عصيفة وهى أذنته

rows.speaker: علقمة بن عبدة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada's verse uses عصيفة for the leaf or foliage of a crop.
rows.anchor: قال علقمة ابن عبدة: تسقى مذانب قد مالت عصيفتها ... حدورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الريحان refers to edible grain and provision; سبحانك وريحانك means “Your provision,” as in al-Namr's verse.
rows.anchor: والريحان الحب منه الذي يؤكل، يقال: سبحانك وريحانك أي رزقك

rows.speaker: النمر بن تولب
rows.claim: Al-Namr ibn Tawlab's verse uses الريحان in the sense of provision.
rows.anchor: قال النمر بن تولب: سماء الإله وريحانه ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mutaffif is someone who fails to give people their full measure.
rows.anchor: «ويل للمطففين» (1) المطفف الذي لا يوفى على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كالوهم and وزنوهم mean measured or weighed for them; Khuffāf's poetry witnesses the construction.
rows.anchor: «وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم» (3) إذا كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم

rows.speaker: خفاف
rows.claim: Khuffāf's verse is cited as evidence for the object suffix in the meaning “for them.”
rows.anchor: قال خفاف: يصيدك قافلا والمخ رار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سجين means a prison; the pattern is derived from السجن like فسيق from الفسق.
rows.anchor: «لفي سجين » (7) فى حبس، فعيل من السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرقوم means written or recorded.
rows.anchor: «مرقوم» (9) مكتوب.. «كلا بل ران على قلوبهم» (14)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ران means it overpowered or covered the heart, as wine covers a drunkard's mind and death covers a dead person.
rows.anchor: «كلا بل ران على قلوبهم» (14) غلب على قلبه والخمر ترين

rows.speaker: أبو زبيد
rows.claim: Abū Zubayd's poem says wine came over a person, illustrating the verb ران.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زبيد: ثم لما رآه رانت به الخم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نضرة النعيم uses نضرة as a verbal noun from ناضرة.
rows.anchor: «نضرة النعيم» (24) مصدر «ناضرة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رحيق is a pure drink without adulteration, whether musk or wine.
rows.anchor: «رحيق» (25) الرحيق (25) الذي ليس فيه غش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مختوم means sealed, and عاقبة ريح describes its lasting or final aroma.
rows.anchor: «مختوم» (25) له ختام. عاقبة ريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ختامه means its end or outcome.
rows.anchor: «مختوم» (25) له ختام. عاقبة ريح. «ختامه» (26) عاقبته..
